category_info.fruit_size_at_harvest: 6-9 cm in diameter depending on cultivar
category_info.ripening_signs: Skin turns characteristic color, fruit easily separates when twisted upward, seeds inside turn dark brown
category_info.pollination: Most cultivars require cross-pollination from a different compatible apple or crabapple cultivar blooming concurrently
category_info.pruning_season: Late winter while dormant; optional light summer thinning for canopy airflow
category_info.watering_need: Moderate; approx 2.5 cm of water per week for established trees, more during fruit sizing in dry periods
category_info.sunlight_need: Full sun (6-8+ hours of direct sunlight daily)

observations.location: Upper leaf surface, centered along the primary midrib and secondary veins
observations.evidence: Faint, irregular dark olive-brown discolorations radiating along leaf veins
Subtle puckering and loss of uniform sheen where discoloration clusters

possible_causes.name: Apple scab (Venturia inaequalis)
possible_causes.reason: The irregular, diffuse olive-green to dark brown velvety spots appearing along the main and secondary veins on the upper surface are hallmark early symptoms of Venturia inaequalis infection.

possible_causes.name: Early fungal leaf spot (e.g., Marssonina leaf blotch or Alternaria)
possible_causes.reason: Other foliar pathogens can initiate small dark lesions on apple foliage, though they typically form more circular necrotic spots rather than vein-associated velvety patches.

recommended_actions.action: Ensure overhead watering is avoided and water only at the soil line
recommended_actions.reason: Apple scab spores require prolonged leaf wetness to germinate and spread across the canopy.

recommended_actions.action: Prune interior dense shoots during dry weather to increase canopy airflow and sun penetration
recommended_actions.reason: Good ventilation hastens leaf drying after rain, suppressing secondary spore proliferation.

recommended_actions.action: Collect and destroy or compost fallen leaves thoroughly at the end of the season
recommended_actions.reason: Venturia inaequalis overwinters primarily in fallen infected foliage from which spring ascospores are released.

seasonal_context: Apple scab primary infections typically occur during cool, wet spring weather when buds and young leaves are emerging.
what_to_monitor: Expansion or darkening of lesions into distinct velvety, olive-black scabby patches
Similar dark scabby lesions appearing on developing fruit surfaces
limitations: Only a single excised leaf against an artificial background is visible, making whole-canopy incidence and fruit involvement impossible to assess directly.
follow_up_questions: Are these spots present across the entire tree or isolated to a few leaves?
Has the region experienced prolonged rainy or humid conditions over the past 2-3 weeks?
